preamble: The Middle Korean vowel ㆍ (arae-a), reconstructed as [ʌ], was lost from almost all modern Korean varieties; while it usually became [a] in first syllables and [ɨ] elsewhere, a number of words rounded it to [o]. Standard Korean shows this in 소매 'sleeve' from Middle Korean ᄉᆞᄆᆡ /sʌ.mʌj/, and Jeolla, Gyeongsang, Chungcheong and Hamgyong dialects round it after the labial ㅍ, as in 포리 'fly' beside standard 파리 (Middle Korean ᄑᆞ리) and Gyeongsang 퐅 'red bean' beside standard 팥 (Middle Korean ᄑᆞᇧ).

examples.note: The first-syllable arae-a became [o] in the standard language, where most such words have [a].
Wiktionary attributes the [o] to rounding after the labial ㅍ; the form is recorded for Jeolla, Gyeongsang, Chungcheong, Hamgyong and Yukjin dialects.

examples.to: Gyeongsang 퐅 pot 'red bean' (standard 팥 pat)
examples.note: Same rounding of arae-a after the labial ㅍ; the standard language has [a].

period: Late Middle Korean to Modern Korean
